name: Mark Alexander Boyd
bio: Mark Alexander Boyd (1563–1601) was a Scottish soldier and scholar who spent much of his life on the Continent and wrote Latin verse.
He is remembered chiefly for a single sonnet in Scots, “Fra bank to bank, fra wood to wood I rin.”

poems.title: Sonet
poems.author: Mark Alexander Boyd
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of English Verse (1900)
poems.text:
Fra bank to bank, fra wood to wood I rin,
  Ourhailit with my feeble fantasie;
  Like til a leaf that fallis from a tree,
Or til a reed ourblawin with the win.

Twa gods guides me: the ane of tham is blin,
  Yea and a bairn brocht up in vanitie;
  The next a wife ingenrit of the sea,
And lichter nor a dauphin with her fin.

Unhappy is the man for evermair
  That tills the sand and sawis in the air;
  But twice unhappier is he, I lairn,
That feidis in his hairt a mad desire,
And follows on a woman throw the fire,
  Led by a blind and teachit by a bairn.
